name: Villa Medicea di Careggi

dates.built: 1417 acquired; remodelled by Michelozzo from the 1450s
dates.note: ICOMOS says only that the villa 'was acquired by the Medici in 1417' and was 'rearranged by Michelozzo'. The node's own exemplar entry gives 1457 and says the remodelling is 'conventionally dated to the 1450s'; the English Wikipedia article gives 'Construction started c. 1325' for the earlier fabric. No single build date is asserted here.

refs.title: Medici Villas and Gardens in Tuscany - UNESCO World Heritage Centre
refs.note: The serial inscription of 2013, criteria (ii)(iv)(vi), which covers twelve villas and two gardens; this building is one component of it. The Italian Ministry of Culture's UNESCO office page for the same property prints 'Ref 175', 'Date of Inscription 2013', 'Property 125.4 ha' and 'Buffer zone 3,539.08 ha'.

survey.prepared: ICOMOS evaluation of nomination No 175, 'Medici Villas and Gardens (Italy)', prepared for the World Heritage Committee; the report prints 'Date of ICOMOS approval of this report 6 March 2013'.

quotes.text: Part 3: The Villa di Careggi (Florence) was acquired by the Medici in 1417, north of Florence.
quotes.page: ICOMOS evaluation No 175, section 2 'The property - Description', Part 3; the span read continues 'Like the previous' and was cut there by the extractor.

quotes.text: Like the previous villas, it was rearranged by Michelozzo and its general structure and its architectural motifs still closely reflected the late medieval spirit, notably through the stylistic use of a crenelated overhanging parapet. For the first time, a relationship between the villa and its surrounding countryside was deliberately sought by the removal of walls in order to open up perspectives. It has one of the first examples of a loggia decorated with arabesques.
quotes.page: ICOMOS evaluation No 175, Part 3; read in a second extract of the same document with a different query, which returned this span and not the one above.

quotes.text: Two porticoes show a Renaissance style: the western one opens onto a lawn overlooking the surrounding landscape. The internal courtyard has two galleries. The villa has fine interior decoration dating back to several periods of occupation by the Medici. There is a garden in front of the main facade and a large landscaped park surrounding the villa on all sides. Today, it lies at the edge of a hospital complex, of which it was a part until 2000.
quotes.page: ICOMOS evaluation No 175, Part 3, the span that closes it; the extract prints the c-cedilla of 'facade' as an accented character, transcribed here without it.

note: Tranche 3, Italian rural vernacular cluster, 5 September 2026. The three quotes are three separate extract spans of one document and are deliberately NOT joined: the first ends where the extractor cut it, and the second begins with the words that follow. Careggi is the villa where the evaluation records the loggia being opened deliberately onto the countryside, which is the feature this node's own kit binds a loggia rule for.
